summary: sextant-cli-linux-arm64 ships opaque Go binary implementing a WebRTC remote-control agent with mismatched 'claude_control' publisher identity
details: The tarball contains a single 12MB stripped linux/arm64 ELF at bin/sxt (sha256 2db6f82e5721f8784115a12dba389fc7cacdcf7a349f9d9e2e6c1a886b9928ca) and a 236-byte package.json — no source, README, LICENSE file, checksum, or build metadata. The binary statically links the full pion WebRTC stack (webrtc/v4, dtls, ice, turn, stun, sctp, datachannel), coder/websocket, and skip2/go-qrcode — the canonical component set for a QR-paired, WebRTC-signaled remote-control agent capable of NAT traversal into the host that runs it. package.json advertises the package as 'Sextant (sxt) binary for linux/arm64', but its license field points to an unrelated repository: 'SEE LICENSE IN https://github.com/ddos798/claude_control'. The publisher-identity mismatch, the 'ddos'/'claude_control' naming, the platform-optional-package distribution shape that hides the payload from source review, and the WebRTC agent library fingerprint together describe a remote-control channel over WebRTC/WebSocket into the installer's host rather than a legitimate prebuilt CLI. Invocation of bin/sxt by the parent sextant-cli wrapper opens a network-sourced command channel to the installer's machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
